frames.u: Check your account, not their phone

frames.b: Overpaid and asked for a refund?

reel1.caption:
A screenshot is not payment.

Wait until the money actually shows in your account before you hand over goods or finish the job. Screenshots can be edited, and a buyer who overpays and asks you to refund the difference is a known scam.

Save this before your next sale.

#smallbusinessSA #entrepreneurSA #sidehustleSA #lekkerhustle

reel2.caption:
No deposit, no booked date.

For cakes, custom work or any job where you buy materials first, take a deposit to secure the order, get the balance before delivery and send a simple receipt each time. If they cancel, your costs are covered.

Send this to a friend who is starting out.

slides.title: Know what sells
slides.head: Look at last month before you buy.
slides.body: Sort items into fast sellers, slow sellers and dead stock. Fast sellers get your cash first.

slides.title: Set a stock budget
slides.head: Decide how much cash may go into stock.
slides.body: Keep separate pots for stock, running costs and your own pay, so stock does not eat the rent money.

slides.title: Buy small, buy often
slides.head: A bulk discount only helps if you sell the bulk.
slides.body: Saving R2 a unit is a bad deal if your cash sits on the shelf for months.

slides.title: Use deposits
slides.head: The safest stock is already sold.
slides.body: For items you do not carry, take a deposit first, then buy. Their deposit pays for your stock.

slides.title: Talk to your supplier
slides.head: Ask for smaller quantities or swaps.
slides.body: Only take credit if you are sure you can pay on the due date.

slides.title: Clear slow stock
slides.head: Dead stock is money already spent.
slides.body: Bundle it with a fast seller or discount it, then do not reorder it.
